blocks.text: Your cloud deployment infrastructure might change over time to meet your business needs. You might:

blocks.item: Want to change business units for cloud accounts that serve a different purpose.
Have removed a cloud account or no longer want ZPC to scan configuration metadata for a specific cloud account.
Have removed Kubernetes clusters in your cloud deployments.

blocks.text: You can address such changes on the Zscaler Posture Control Admin Portal.

blocks.heading: Changing Business Units for Multiple Cloud Accounts

blocks.text: To change business units for multiple cloud accounts:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Cloud Accounts, then click the Accounts tab.
Select the checkboxes for the cloud accounts you want to manage.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: Click the Actions drop-down menu, then click Change Business Unit.
Select the business unit you want to move the cloud accounts to from the drop-down menu.
Mark the I understand the consequences and want to proceed checkbox.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: Click Apply.

blocks.text: To offboard a cloud account from ZPC:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Cloud Accounts, then click the Accounts tab.
Click the Actions drop-down menu for the cloud account you want to offboard, then click the Delete Account button.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: Mark the I understand the consequences and want to proceed checkbox.
Click Delete.

blocks.text: See image.
You can also choose to delete an organization and all the accounts in the organization. To delete an organization:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Cloud Accounts, then click the Organization tab.
Click the Actions drop-down menu for the organization you want to offboard, then click the Delete Organization button.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: Mark the I understand the consequences and want to proceed checkbox.
Click Delete.

blocks.text: See image.
You can remove a Kubernetes Cluster from your cloud service provider and stop ZPC from scanning configuration metadata for the cluster. To offboard a Kubernetes cluster:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Cloud Accounts.
Select Kubernetes.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: In the Actions column, click the Delete icon for the cluster you want to delete.
In the confirmation pop-up, click Delete.

blocks.text: See image.
If you want to delete multiple clusters:

blocks.item: Select the clusters you want to delete, then click Actions > Delete.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: In the confirmation pop-up, click Delete.

blocks.text: After you offboard a Kubernetes cluster, you need to remove the additional permissions ZPC has on your cloud service provider:

blocks.item: EKS Clusters
AKS Clusters
GKE Clusters

blocks.text: On the AWS Management Console, run the following commands on the AWS CloudShell:

blocks.item: eksctl delete iamidentitymapping --arn <zscalerRoleARN>
kubectl delete clusterrolebindings zpc-reader
kubectl delete clusterrole zpc-read-role

On the Microsoft Azure Portal, run the following commands on the Azure Powershell:

blocks.item: Delete the Azure Kubernetes Service Cluster User Role:

az role assignment delete --assignee “<service-principal-id>” --role “Azure Kubernetes Service Cluster User Role” --scope "/subscriptions/<subscriptionId>/resourceGroups/<resourceGroup>/providers/Microsoft.ContainerService/ManagedClusters/<cluster>"
Delete ZPC's cluster role binding:
kubectl delete clusterrolebindings zpc-reader-"<$servicePrincipalObjectId>"
Run the following command to get your Service Principal Object ID:
az ad sp show --id <ZPC-Service-Principal-Id> --query id --out tsv"
